facts.statement: A study found people who drank five or more cups of coffee daily had a 47% lower risk of developing liver cancer compared to non-coffee drinkers.
facts.support: The study analyzed data on nearly 355,000 adults and tracked them for about 13 years.

facts.statement: Coffee-drinkers had lower levels of liver inflammation and healthier liver function markers than non-coffee drinkers.
facts.support: Researchers observed these benefits in both regular and decaf coffee consumers.

facts.statement: A study found that drinking five or more cups of coffee daily could reduce the risk of liver cancer by 47%.
facts.support: The Cedars-Sinai Medical Center study showed a 47% lower risk of liver cancer for those consuming five or more cups per day compared with non-coffee drinkers.

facts.statement: Coffee consumption is associated with healthier liver scans and blood protein patterns.
facts.support: Participants who drank coffee had less fat, inflammation, and scarring in their livers as shown by MRI scans and blood tests.

facts.statement: Consuming five or more cups of coffee daily reduces liver cancer risk by 47% according to UK Biobank study data.
facts.support: UK Biobank tracked over 350,000 individuals and found a 47% reduced liver cancer risk in those drinking five or more cups of coffee daily.

facts.statement: Coffee consumption lowers the risk of cirrhosis by approximately 32% regardless of caffeine content.
facts.support: The protective effect was observed for both caffeinated and decaffeinated coffee, indicating other compounds may be responsible.

facts.statement: A new study suggests that drinking up to five cups of coffee daily may reduce liver cancer risk by 47%.
facts.support: The findings indicate that people who drank five or more cups of coffee a day had the greatest reduction in liver cancer risk.

facts.statement: Coffee consumption was associated with lower risks of liver disease and liver-related death.
facts.support: Researchers found that higher coffee intake correlated with significantly lower risks of liver disease, liver cancer, and liver-related death.

facts.statement: Drinking 5 cups of coffee daily may cut liver cancer risk by 47% according to a study.
facts.support: A new study suggests regular coffee consumption may support liver health and significantly lower the risk of liver disease and liver cancer when consumed consistently.

facts.statement: Coffee is linked to improved liver health and reduced risk of liver disease.
facts.support: The study found that regular coffee consumption reduces the risk of liver disease and liver cancer, by up to five cups of coffee a day.

facts.statement: Coffee consumption is associated with a 47% reduction in liver cancer risk according to the study.
facts.support: The source mentions that drinking five or more cups daily correlates with a 47% lower risk of liver cancer.

facts.statement: Drinking one to two cups of coffee daily reduces cirrhosis risk by 20%.
facts.support: The text states that one to two cups daily was linked with a 20% lower risk of cirrhosis.

facts.statement: Drinking 5+ cups of coffee daily is associated with nearly 50% lower liver cancer risk.
facts.support: A new study found higher coffee consumption correlates with reduced cirrhosis, liver cancer risks, and liver-related death.

facts.statement: Coffee may reduce the risk of chronic diseases and boost longevity.
facts.support: Research published earlier this year linked coffee to reduced chronic disease risk and increased longevity.

facts.statement: Decaffeinated coffee provides nearly the same liver protection as regular coffee.
facts.support: The research indicates that decaf offers similar benefits, suggesting caffeine is not the primary active ingredient responsible for liver health improvements.

warnings: The study shows an association, not proof that coffee directly prevents liver disease
Findings are observational and not proof of causation
Results need validation in more diverse populations
Associations do not imply direct cause-and-effect
